lower_bound.quote: Let $T$ be a minimal (under inclusion) transversal of $\mathcal C$. For each $i$, $a_i\in S_\infty$ is a multiple of some $\pi(t)$ with $t\in\mathcal C$; then $t\subseteq\mathrm{supp}(a_i)$, and $T$ meeting $t$ implies $T$ meets $\mathrm{supp}(a_i)$. Hence $\pi(T)\in S_\infty$
lower_bound.witness: NON-SEQUITUR: The premises establish only that T, possibly infinite, meets every support. They do not establish that T is finite, although π(T) was defined only for finite sets. This is a genuine possibility: for distinct odd primes x_n, the intersecting antichain C={{2,x_n}:n≥1} has the infinite minimal transversal T={x_n:n≥1}; deleting x_k leaves {2,x_k} unhit. Thus π(T) need not be an integer, so Claim 3.2 is not proved for all minimal transversals.
lower_bound.load_bearing: Step 4(c) obtains a minimal transversal by Zorn inside the infinite set I∪Z_ω, so that transversal may be infinite. Applying self-duality there is essential to proving C finite and hence that membership depends on finitely many primes.

parsed.notes: The enumeration characterization and the conditional period assembly from the first term are valid. The gap is the unproved extension of self-duality to infinite minimal transversals, which breaks the claimed finiteness argument.
